name: Lint

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: lint-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  lint:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
          cache: pip
          cache-dependency-path: .pre-commit-config.yaml

      - name: Install pre-commit
        run: python -m pip install pre-commit

      - name: Cache pre-commit environments
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/pre-commit
          key: pre-commit|${{ env.pythonLocation }}|${{ hashFiles('.pre-commit-config.yaml') }}

      # no-commit-to-branch guards local commits; CI also runs on pushes to main.
      - name: Run pre-commit checks
        run: SKIP=no-commit-to-branch pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure

[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools>=64"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

[project]
name = "sgl-amd-mono"
version = "0.1.0.dev0"
description = "Monokernels for SGLang on AMD Instinct GPUs"
readme = "README.md"
license = { text = "Apache-2.0" }
requires-python = ">=3.10"

sgl_amd_mono = "sgl_amd_mono:register_specs"

[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
include = ["sgl_amd_mono*"]

# SGLang-AMD-Mono

## Introduction

**SGLang-AMD-Mono** is the monokernel library of the [SGLang](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang) framework for AMD Instinct GPUs. A monokernel is a persistent kernel that runs most of a decoder layer, including its attention, its mixture-of-experts block and both tensor-parallel all-reduces, in one or two launches. This removes the launch gaps and collective latency that dominate small-batch decoding.

The library implements SGLang's monokernel interface ([RFC #43949](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/43949)) and loads as an SGLang [general plugin](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/docs/docs/hardware-platforms/plugin.mdx) (the `sglang.srt.plugins` entry point), which registers each model's spec under the monokernel backend `amd`. With `--monokernel-backend amd`, every decode and speculative-verify step that a spec serves runs on its kernels, and every other step runs SGLang's standard path.

> **Experimental:** `--monokernel-backend` is an experimental SGLang feature. The kernels, the models and setups they cover, and the plugin interface may change.

## Features

### Supported Models

| Model | GPU | Tensor parallel | Coverage |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash | MI350X, MI355X (gfx950) | 2, 4 | All 40 layers in decode and DSpark verify steps of up to 48 rows, and the DSpark draft stages |
| GLM-5.3-Flash | MI355X (gfx950) | 2, 4, 8 | 41 of the 42 MoE layers, all but the last (one launch each), in decode steps of up to 8 rows (4 at TP2) |
| GLM-5.3 | MI355X (gfx950) | 4, 8 | All 75 MoE layers (one launch each), in decode steps of up to 8 rows (4 at TP4) |
| MiniMax-M3 (MXFP4) | MI350X, MI355X (gfx950) | 4 | The 57 sparse MoE layers in decode and EAGLE3 verify steps of up to 16 rows |

### Design

- **One or two launches per layer.** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash runs two. K1 runs the attention's input mixing and projections and writes the KV cache. K2 runs the sparse attention, the output projections, the FFN mixing, the MoE and both all-reduces. On the indexer layers, K2i runs between them: it scores the FP4 index keys in one launch, and SGLang's top-k kernels select each row's top-k from its logits. GLM-5.3-Flash and GLM-5.3 run each covered layer as one launch. MiniMax-M3 runs one too: K1 (the input norm, the fused qkv and index projection, the q / k norms, RoPE, the KV and index-key writes and the index scores) runs in front of the block selection, the sparse attention, o_proj, the router, the MoE and both all-reduces, in one launch.
- **Graph-safe routing.** Each step is routed by its CUDA graph key alone, so every rank makes the same decision and a captured graph replays the decision made at capture.
- **Fail-stop synchronization.** Every wait on another workgroup or GPU has a deadline. A failed wait stops the launch on every rank, so no token from a failed step is returned.
- **In-place weights.** The kernels read the weights SGLang loaded. The few weights that need another layout or precision (MiniMax-M3's attention projections run in FP8) are copied once at startup, and each copy is logged.

## Quick Start

### Requirements

- SGLang with the monokernel interface (`sglang.srt.monokernels`, in review as [sgl-project/sglang#44353](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44353))
- ROCm with FlyDSL and AITER, as included in SGLang's ROCm images
- AMD Instinct MI350X or MI355X
- MiniMax-M3 also needs SGLang's page16 SHUFFLE K / V for AITER sparse attention ([sgl-project/sglang#41998](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/41998), on [#41708](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/41708)). Until both merge, `--monokernel-backend amd` refuses MiniMax-M3 and names them.

### Installation

```bash
git clone https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-amd-mono.git
cd sgl-amd-mono
pip install -e .
```

### Usage

```bash
SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --tp 4 \
  --speculative-algorithm DSPARK \
  --speculative-dspark-block-size 5 \
  --fp8-gemm-backend aiter \
  --enforce-shared-experts-fusion \
  --monokernel-backend amd
```

On gfx950 the decode graph capture fails in AITER's MoE without
`AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0`. The flags are those of the serving tests
(`test/e2e/deepseek_v41_server.py`).

MiniMax-M3, with an EAGLE3 draft:

```bash
SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 SGLANG_MINIMAX_M3_INDEX_TOPK_FREQ=1 python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 \
  --tp 4 \
  --quantization quark \
  --attention-backend aiter \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --page-size 128 \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE3 \
  --speculative-draft-model-path Inferact/MiniMax-M3-EAGLE3-GQA \
  --speculative-num-steps 3 \
  --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
  --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \
  --monokernel-backend amd
```

If the model, GPU or configuration is not supported, the server refuses to start and lists every reason.

## Repository Structure

```text
sgl-amd-mono/
├── sgl_amd_mono/
│   ├── common/          # HIP device runtime: guarded waits, epochs, peer memory
│   ├── deepseek_v41/
│   │   ├── spec.py      # target model: spec and forward
│   │   ├── draft.py     # DSpark draft model: spec and forward
│   │   └── gfx950/      # kernels and launch runner
│   ├── glm53_flash/
│   │   ├── spec.py      # spec and forward
│   │   ├── check.py     # SGLANG_AMD_MONO_CHECK: each layer against SGLang's own
│   │   └── gfx950/      # kernels and launch runner
│   ├── glm53/
│   │   ├── spec.py      # spec and forward
│   │   ├── check.py     # SGLANG_AMD_MONO_CHECK: each layer against SGLang's own
│   │   └── gfx950/      # kernels and launch runner
│   └── minimax_m3/
│       ├── spec.py      # spec and forward
│       ├── weights.py   # the layer views the kernels read
│       └── gfx950/      # kernels and launch runner
└── test/
    ├── unit/            # CPU: the specs and the SGLang interface contract
    ├── kernels/         # GPU: each launch against SGLang's reference ops
    └── e2e/             # GPU: serving accuracy and fault injection
```

## Testing

```bash
pytest test/unit                                                # CPU only
pytest test/kernels test/e2e -k "not glm53 and not minimax_m3"  # 4 x MI350X or MI355X, DEEPSEEK_V41_FLASH_MODEL_PATH set
pytest test/kernels test/e2e -k glm53_flash                     # GLM_53_FLASH_MODEL_PATH set: kernels on 8 GPUs, server at TP4
pytest test/e2e -k "glm53 and not glm53_flash"                  # GLM_53_MODEL_PATH set: server at TP8
pytest test/kernels test/e2e -k minimax_m3                      # 4 x MI350X or MI355X, MINIMAX_M3_MODEL_PATH and MINIMAX_M3_EAGLE3_PATH set
```

## Contributing

Format code with [pre-commit](https://pre-commit.com/) (`pre-commit install`). Every module that reads SGLang internals declares them in `SGLANG_READS`. `test/unit/test_contract.py` checks each declared name against the installed SGLang, so an incompatible SGLang change fails on CPU.

"""K2i's per-step score tasks on CPU (RFC #43949): ``index_plan`` lays out the
scorer's tasks from the rows' column bounds alone, and the kernel calls the same
functions on traced values. On Python ints and random steps: the host walk plan
fits the grid and covers every scored row's chunks exactly once, and a candidate
consumer's tasks tile its chunks."""

import numpy as np
import pytest

from sgl_amd_mono.common.plan import BLOCKS
from sgl_amd_mono.deepseek_v41.gfx950.indexer import index_plan as ip

BOUNDS = [0, 1, 300, 511, 512, 513, 640, 8191, 8192, 8193, 16384, 16385, 20000,
          131071, 131072, 131073, 524288, (1 << 20) + 96]  # fmt: skip


def _step(*, rng, n):
    """A step's rows: requests of 1 (decode), 6 (DSpark verify) or ragged rows,
    each request's rows seeing one more column than the row before."""
    kind = rng.integers(3)
    owners, bounds, row = [], [], 0
    while row < n:
        size = 1 if kind == 0 else 6 if kind == 1 else int(rng.integers(1, 9))
        size = min(size, n - row)
        ctx = int(rng.choice(BOUNDS + [int(rng.integers(0, 1 << 20))]))
        owners += [row] * size
        bounds += [max(ctx - (size - 1 - r), 0) for r in range(size)]
        row += size
    return np.array(bounds, dtype=np.int64), np.array(owners, dtype=np.int64)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("seed", range(3))
def test_walk_plan_covers_each_scored_chunk_once(seed):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    for _ in range(300):
        n = int(rng.integers(1, 49))
        bounds, owners = _step(rng=rng, n=n)
        plan = np.full((BLOCKS, 4), -1, dtype=np.int64)
        ip.fill_walk_plan(bounds=bounds, owners=owners, plan=plan)
        live = plan[:, 1] > 0
        k = int(live.sum())
        assert live[:k].all() and (plan[k:] == 0).all(), plan[: k + 2]
        covered = {}
        for lead, span, ch0, ch1 in plan[:k].tolist():
            assert 0 < span <= ip.WALK_ROWS and 0 <= ch0 < ch1, (lead, span, ch0, ch1)
            assert len(set(owners[lead : lead + span].tolist())) == 1  # one table
            covered.setdefault((lead, span), []).append((ch0, ch1))
        pieces = {}
        for (lead, span), ranges in covered.items():
            ranges.sort()
            # the piece's tasks tile its chunks: [0, its rows' most) exactly once
            need = max(ip.score_chunks(int(b)) for b in bounds[lead : lead + span])
            assert ranges[0][0] == 0 and ranges[-1][1] == need, (ranges, need)
            assert all(a[1] == b[0] for a, b in zip(ranges, ranges[1:])), ranges
            for t in range(lead, lead + span):
                assert t not in pieces, t  # each row in one piece
                pieces[t] = need
        for t, b in enumerate(bounds.tolist()):
            # a scored row's chunks are all walked; a row seeing <= TOPK is not scored
            if ip.scored(b):
                assert pieces.get(t, 0) >= ip.score_chunks(b), (t, b)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("rows", range(1, 49))
def test_a_consumer_tiles_its_candidate_chunks(rows):
    per = ip.reindex_split(rows, BLOCKS, 4)  # a wave's step at least a task
    assert rows * per <= BLOCKS
    spans = [ip.reindex_chunks(i, per) for i in range(per)]
    assert spans[0][0] == 0 and spans[-1][1] == ip.REINDEX_CHUNKS
    assert all(a[1] == b[0] for a, b in zip(spans, spans[1:]))
    assert all(ch1 - ch0 >= 4 for ch0, ch1 in spans)

"""The DeepSeek-V4.1 gfx950 monokernel spec on CPU (RFC #43949): the layers its
forward covers on the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash layer structure, its registry entry, its
per-output bounds and its model refusal reasons. SGLang checks its declared
requirements, the same way for every spec."""

from types import SimpleNamespace

import torch
from sglang.srt.monokernels import spec as registry

import sgl_amd_mono
from sgl_amd_mono.deepseek_v41 import CANDIDATES, HF_CONFIG, draft
from sgl_amd_mono.deepseek_v41 import spec as dsv41

# DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash's layer structure (its config.json)
FLASH = SimpleNamespace(
    num_hidden_layers=40,
    compress_ratios=[0, 0] + [2] * 18 + [1] * 20 + [0, 0, 0],
    kv_source_layer_ids=[2, 8, 14, 20],
    index_source_layer_ids=[2, 8, 14, 20, 24, 28, 32, 36],
    engram_layer_ids=[1, 14],
    **HF_CONFIG,
    model_type="deepseek_v41",
    architectures=["DeepseekV4ForCausalLM"],
)


def test_the_forward_covers_every_flash_layer():
    # the first layer, the Engram layers, the index sources (their compressor and
    # indexer between the launches) and DSpark's target layers (37-39) too
    assert dsv41._covered_layers(FLASH) == list(range(40))


def test_other_layers_have_no_kernels():
    hashed = SimpleNamespace(**{**vars(FLASH), "num_hash_layers": 4})
    assert dsv41._covered_layers(hashed) == list(range(4, 40))  # hash-routed MoE
    ratio4 = SimpleNamespace(**{**vars(FLASH), "compress_ratios": [4] * 43})
    assert dsv41._covered_layers(ratio4) == []  # another compress ratio


def test_the_plugin_registers_both_specs():
    # what SGLang's load_plugins() runs, from the sglang.srt.plugins entry point
    sgl_amd_mono.register_specs()
    for arch, spec in (
        ("DeepseekV4ForCausalLM", dsv41.SPEC),
        ("DeepseekV4ForCausalLMDSpark", draft.SPEC),
    ):
        found, why = registry.find_spec(
            backend=sgl_amd_mono.BACKEND, architectures=[arch], isa="gfx950"
        )
        assert found is spec, why


def test_kv_records_are_bit_exact():
    # the normal path reads the KV the kernels write (a prefill, a batch past the
    # largest width), so the kernel checks hold K1's KV records to bit-exact
    for spec in (dsv41.SPEC, draft.SPEC):
        assert spec.numerics.bound("k1.kv.max_abs") == 0.0


def _layer(i, **attn):
    attn = {
        "compressor": None,
        "indexer": None,
        "q_head_norm": False,
        "fuse_wqa_wkv": True,
        "n_local_heads": 16,
        "compress_ratio": 0 if i < 2 else 2 if i < 20 else 1,
        **{lin: SimpleNamespace() for lin in ("wqkv_a", "wq_b", "wo_a", "wo_b")},
        **attn,
    }
    experts = SimpleNamespace(w13_weight=SimpleNamespace(is_shuffled=True))
    return SimpleNamespace(
        hc_boundary_fused=True,
        engram=None,
        self_attn=SimpleNamespace(**attn),
        mlp=SimpleNamespace(is_nextn=False, is_hash=False, experts=experts),
    )


def test_model_reasons(monkeypatch):
    import sglang.srt.runtime_context as rc

    monkeypatch.setattr(rc, "get_parallel", lambda: SimpleNamespace(tp_size=4))
    layers = [_layer(i) for i in range(40)]
    model = SimpleNamespace(model=SimpleNamespace(layers=layers))
    seen = {
        ("shared expert fp8", i, p, k): None
        for i in range(40)
        for p in dsv41._SHARED
        for k in ("weight", "scale")
    }
    assert dsv41.SPEC.model_disable_reasons(model, FLASH, seen) == []
    # an FP8 linear method shuffled layer 5's wo_b in place; layer 1 (window only)
    # has a compressor; layer 7's shared expert never went through the load hook
    layers[5] = _layer(5, wo_b=SimpleNamespace(aiter_bpreshuffled=True))
    layers[1] = _layer(1, compress_ratio=0, compressor=SimpleNamespace())
    seen = {k: v for k, v in seen.items() if k[1] != 7}
    reasons = dsv41.SPEC.model_disable_reasons(model, FLASH, seen)
    assert len(reasons) == 3, reasons
    assert reasons[0].startswith("layer 1: a compressor or indexer at compress ratio 0")
    assert reasons[1].startswith("layer 5: an FP8 linear method reordered")
    assert "(layers [7])" in reasons[2]
    # the forward runs every layer: a model with a layer it has no kernels for
    hashed = SimpleNamespace(**{**vars(FLASH), "num_hash_layers": 2})
    reasons = dsv41.SPEC.model_disable_reasons(model, hashed, seen)
    assert reasons[0].startswith("layers [0, 1]: no kernels"), reasons
    # K2i's indexers: the candidate blocks its REINDEX layers score, and SGLang's
    # decode-row query path, which K2i's query runs
    layers[1], layers[5] = _layer(1), _layer(5)
    seen |= {
        ("shared expert fp8", 7, p, k): None
        for p in dsv41._SHARED
        for k in ("weight", "scale")
    }
    rope = SimpleNamespace(dtype=torch.complex64)
    ix = SimpleNamespace(
        is_candidate_source=True,
        uses_candidates=False,
        weights_proj_hip_max_tokens=64,
        **CANDIDATES,
    )
    layers[20] = _layer(20, indexer=ix, freqs_cis=rope)
    assert dsv41.SPEC.model_disable_reasons(model, FLASH, seen) == []
    other_blocks = SimpleNamespace(**{**vars(ix), "candidate_topk_blocks": 1024})
    layers[20] = _layer(20, indexer=other_blocks, freqs_cis=rope)
    no_gemv = SimpleNamespace(**{**vars(ix), "weights_proj_hip_max_tokens": -1})
    layers[24] = _layer(24, indexer=no_gemv, freqs_cis=rope)
    reasons = dsv41.SPEC.model_disable_reasons(model, FLASH, seen)
    assert [r.split(":")[0] for r in reasons] == ["layer 20", "layer 24"], reasons

class GemmaRMSNorm(torch.nn.Module):
    """Named as SGLang's: the views check the norm's type by name."""

    def __init__(self, n):
        super().__init__()
        self.weight = torch.nn.Parameter(
            torch.empty(n, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="meta")
        )


def _meta(*shape, dtype=torch.bfloat16, **attrs):
    t = torch.empty(*shape, dtype=dtype, device="meta")
    for k, v in attrs.items():
        setattr(t, k, v)
    return t


def _layer(**changes):
    """A sparse M3 decoder layer at TP4, its tensors on the meta device."""
    E = N_ROUTED + 1
    experts = SimpleNamespace(
        moe_ep_rank=0,
        num_local_experts=E,
        num_fused_shared_experts=1,
        top_k=5,
        intermediate_size_per_partition=INTER,
        moe_runner_config=SimpleNamespace(activation="silu"),
        w13_weight=_meta(
            E, 2 * INTER, HIDDEN // 2, dtype=torch.uint8, is_shuffled=True
        ),
        w2_weight=_meta(E, HIDDEN, INTER // 2, dtype=torch.uint8, is_shuffled=True),
        w13_weight_scale=_meta(E, 2 * INTER, HIDDEN // 32, dtype=torch.uint8),
        w2_weight_scale=_meta(E, HIDDEN, INTER // 32, dtype=torch.uint8),
    )
    attn = SimpleNamespace(
        is_sparse_attention_layer=True,
        disable_index_value=True,
        num_heads=LOCAL_Q_HEADS,
        num_kv_heads=1,
        num_idx_heads=1,
        head_dim=HEAD_DIM,
        idx_head_dim=HEAD_DIM,
        rotary_dim=ROTARY_DIM,
        use_gemma_norm=True,
        qk_norm_type="per_head",
        q_norm=GemmaRMSNorm(HEAD_DIM),
        k_norm=GemmaRMSNorm(HEAD_DIM),
        index_q_norm=GemmaRMSNorm(HEAD_DIM),
        index_k_norm=GemmaRMSNorm(HEAD_DIM),
        _fused_qkv_index=SimpleNamespace(weight=_meta(qkv_rows(1), HIDDEN)),
        o_proj=SimpleNamespace(weight=_meta(HIDDEN, O_K)),
        rotary_emb=SimpleNamespace(cos_sin_cache=_meta(1 << 20, ROTARY_DIM)),
        attn=SimpleNamespace(k_scale=None, v_scale=None),
    )
    mlp = SimpleNamespace(
        experts=experts,
        gate=SimpleNamespace(weight=_meta(N_ROUTED, HIDDEN, dtype=torch.float32)),
        e_score_correction_bias=_meta(N_ROUTED, dtype=torch.float32),
    )
    layer = SimpleNamespace(
        is_layer_sparse=True,
        self_attn=attn,
        mlp=mlp,
        input_layernorm=GemmaRMSNorm(HIDDEN),
        post_attention_layernorm=GemmaRMSNorm(HIDDEN),
    )
    for path, value in changes.items():
        owner, name = layer, path
        while "." in name:
            head, name = name.split(".", 1)
            owner = getattr(owner, head)
        setattr(owner, name, value)
    return layer

class _Lm:

        return "the model's forward"


def test_a_step_runs_at_the_next_width_and_tp2_takes_four_rows():
    # a step of fewer rows than a width runs at the next width, the rest pad rows
    assert [flash._width(r) for r in flash.ROWS] == [2, 2, 4, 4, 8, 8, 8, 8]
    # TP2 builds no 8-row launch: a wider step runs the model's own forward
    runtimes = {(w, k): None for w in (2, 4) for k in ("kda", "dsa")}
    layers = {i: SimpleNamespace(i=i) for i in range(3, 44)}

    key = registry.ShapeKey(forward_mode="decode", batch_size=8, tokens_per_request=1)
    out = built.forward(registry.Plan(key=key), "ids", "positions", "batch")
    assert out == "the model's forward"
    assert lm.ran == [("ids", "positions", "batch", None, None)]
    # the first covered layer's identity mix leaves the written streams unchanged

"""The MiniMax-M3 row tables a step's launches read (one GPU): causal verify rows

pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(

def inputs():
    pages = torch.tensor(
        [[1, 2, 3, 4], [7, 4, 9, 3], [10, 11, 12, 13], [6, 2, 8, 5]],
        dtype=torch.int32,
        device="cuda",
    )
    table = (
        pages[:, :, None] * 128 + torch.arange(128, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
    ).reshape(4, 512)
    requests = torch.tensor([3, 1], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
    prefixes = torch.tensor([127, 255], dtype=torch.int64, device="cuda")
    columns = torch.tensor([0, 128, 256, 384], dtype=torch.int64, device="cuda")
    blocks = torch.empty((8, 4), dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
    lengths = torch.empty(8, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
    slots = torch.arange(128, 136, dtype=torch.int64, device="cuda")
    return table, requests, prefixes, columns, blocks, lengths, slots


def test_verify_causal_rows_with_shuffled_pages():
    args = inputs()
    blocks, lengths = prepare_token_rows(
        *args, query_len=4, is_verify=True, max_context_len=512
    )
    assert lengths.tolist() == [128, 129, 130, 131, 256, 257, 258, 259]
    assert blocks.tolist() == [[6, 2, 8, 5]] * 4 + [[7, 4, 9, 3]] * 4


def test_graph_replay_refreshes_prefixes_and_request_mapping():
    args = inputs()
    prepare_token_rows(*args, query_len=4, is_verify=True, max_context_len=512)
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
    with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
        prepare_token_rows(*args, query_len=4, is_verify=True, max_context_len=512)
    args[1].copy_(torch.tensor([0, 2], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"))
    args[2].copy_(torch.tensor([383, 507], dtype=torch.int64, device="cuda"))
    graph.replay()
    assert args[5].tolist() == [384, 385, 386, 387, 508, 509, 510, 511]
    assert args[4].tolist() == [[1, 2, 3, 4]] * 4 + [[10, 11, 12, 13]] * 4

    assert lengths.tolist() == [1, 2, 3, 4, 0, 0, 0, 0]
    assert blocks.tolist() == [[6, 2, 8, 5]] * 4 + [[0, 0, 0, 0]] * 4

a satisfied wait leaves the error words clean, a wait nobody satisfies stops
at its deadline with the ``deadline`` word set, later waits stop at once and
keep a ``peer`` word, the fault injection stalls the named site, and a failed
wait stops the launch (it never runs on)."""

import subprocess
import sys
import time

import pytest
import torch

pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
    not (
        torch.cuda.is_available()
        and torch.version.hip
        and "gfx95" in torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0).gcnArchName
    ),
    reason="needs a gfx950 GPU",
)


def _build(publish: bool, fault_site=None, stop=False):
    import flydsl.compiler as flyc
    import flydsl.expr as fx
    from aiter.ops.flydsl.kernels import buffer_ops as bo
    from flydsl.expr import const_expr
    from flydsl.expr.typing import Int64

    from sgl_amd_mono.common import guard
    from sgl_amd_mono.common.ops import CM_DEV, rsrc
    from sgl_amd_mono.common.plan import THREADS, kernel_sources
    from sgl_amd_mono.common.sync import Mailbox, sreg

    name = f"mono_guard_test_p{int(publish)}_f{fault_site or 0}_s{int(stop)}"
    keyed = (publish, fault_site, stop, kernel_sources(guard.__name__))

    @flyc.kernel(name=name, known_block_size=[THREADS, 1, 1])
    def k(epoch: Int64, box: Int64):
        _ = keyed
        with guard.scope(guard.Guard(epoch, fault_site=fault_site, stop=stop)):
            # held in a dict, as the kernels hold it: traced branches carry IR values only
            c = {"mb": Mailbox(fx.Int32(7))}
            if const_expr(publish):
                if (fx.block_idx.x == 1) & (fx.thread_idx.x == 0):
                    c["mb"].put(sreg(box, 0, "x"), 0, fx.Int32(42))
            got = c["mb"].poll([(sreg(box, 0, "x"), 0, 1)])
            if (fx.block_idx.x == 0) & (fx.thread_idx.x == 0):
                bo.buffer_store(got[0][0], rsrc(box), 2, cache_modifier=CM_DEV)

    @flyc.jit
    def launch(epoch: Int64, box: Int64, stream: fx.Stream = fx.Stream(None)):
        _ = keyed
        k(epoch, box).launch(grid=(2,), block=(THREADS,), stream=stream)

    return launch


def _epoch(deadline_s):
    from sgl_amd_mono.common import guard

    e = torch.zeros(64, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
    ticks = guard.deadline_ticks(deadline_s)
    lo = ticks & 0xFFFFFFFF
    e[guard.GUARD_DEADLINE] = lo - (1 << 32) if lo >= 1 << 31 else lo
    e[guard.GUARD_DEADLINE + 1] = ticks >> 32
    return e


def _words(e):
    from sgl_amd_mono.common import guard

    return [int(e[i]) for i in guard.ERROR_WORDS]


def _run(launch, e, box):
    t = time.monotonic()
    launch(e.data_ptr(), box.data_ptr(), stream=torch.cuda.current_stream())
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    return time.monotonic() - t


def test_satisfied_wait_is_clean():
    e, box = _epoch(5.0), torch.zeros(4, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
    _run(_build(publish=True), e, box)
    assert _words(e) == [0, 0, 0]
    assert int(box[2]) == 42


def test_unsatisfied_wait_returns_at_its_deadline_and_later_waits_at_once():
    e, box = _epoch(0.3), torch.zeros(4, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
    took = _run(_build(publish=False), e, box)
    deadline, peer, fault = _words(e)
    assert deadline == 2 and fault == 0, _words(e)  # site 1, stored as 1 + site
    assert 0.25 < took < 30, took
    # a later launch's waits see the failure and return at once
    box.zero_()
    took = _run(_build(publish=False), e, box)
    assert took < 0.25, took
    assert _words(e)[1] == 1  # the peer word: it stopped on a failure elsewhere


def test_fault_injection_stalls_the_named_site():
    e, box = _epoch(0.3), torch.zeros(4, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
    _run(_build(publish=True, fault_site=1), e, box)
    assert _words(e)[0] == 2, _words(e)


def _stop_child():
    """A wait nobody satisfies, with the stop on: the launch must not return."""
    e, box = _epoch(0.2), torch.zeros(4, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
    _run(_build(publish=False, stop=True), e, box)
    print("RETURNED", flush=True)

stops the server before any token of the failed step is sent. Every backbone layer
runs whole; the kernel checks cover each form of K1's input and each kind of K2i
launch."""

LAUNCH_TIMEOUT = 3600
# The normal path scores 0.88 to 0.91 on this recipe: the bound is for gross failures
GSM8K_BOUND = 0.85
# Decode against prefill on 8 LongBench-v2 prompts, mean KL: about 0.007 on the
# normal path, 0.011 with the monokernels (up to 0.022 for one prompt)
KL_BOUND = 0.03
# Prompts past the candidate span (2048 blocks of 8 positions): every step's index
# sources run two-level. Their lengths, in tokens, and the bound on their mean KL:
# about 0.026 on the normal path, 0.030 with the monokernels (DSpark; a prompt's
# own KL ranges 0.0001 to 0.08 on either path)
LONG_PROMPT_TOKENS = (18000, 21000, 24000, 27000)
LONG_KL_BOUND = 0.06
# long enough that most of its tokens come from decode or verify steps, not the prefill
PASSKEY = "4861372950"


def _logprobs(*, input_ids, max_new_tokens, logprob_start_len):
    """Greedy /generate of every prompt from an empty cache, with logprobs."""
    url = DEFAULT_URL_FOR_TEST
    requests.post(
        url + "/flush_cache", params={"timeout": 30}, timeout=40
    ).raise_for_status()
    r = requests.post(
        url + "/generate",
        json={
            "input_ids": input_ids,
            "sampling_params": {
                "temperature": 0.0,
                "max_new_tokens": max_new_tokens,
                "ignore_eos": True,
            },
            "return_logprob": True,
            "return_text_in_logprobs": False,
            "logprob_start_len": logprob_start_len,
        },
        timeout=3600,
    )
    r.raise_for_status()
    return r.json()


def _long_prompts():
    """Long prompts of natural text: LongBench-v2 prompts (the KL test's, about
    3000 tokens each, cached) joined end to end."""
    ids = get_input_ids(tokenizer_path=MODEL, num_samples=48, trust_remote_code=True)
    text = [t for p in ids for t in p]  # (the KL test's prompts carry no BOS)
    out, at = [], 0
    for n in LONG_PROMPT_TOKENS:
        out.append(text[at : at + n])
        at += n // 2  # overlapping windows: the corpus is about 140K tokens
    assert all(len(p) == n for p, n in zip(out, LONG_PROMPT_TOKENS)), "corpus too short"
    return out


def _launch(args=ARGS, extra_env=None, extra_args=(), log=None):
    env = {**os.environ, **ENV, **(extra_env or {})}
    return popen_launch_server(
        MODEL,
        DEFAULT_URL_FOR_TEST,
        timeout=LAUNCH_TIMEOUT,
        other_args=args + ["--monokernel-backend", BACKEND, *extra_args],
        env=env,
        return_stdout_stderr=log,
    )


class _Serving:
    """A server's switch points: ``PARALLEL`` requests at a time step past the
    largest covered width as the batch fills, and back as it drains."""

    SERVER_ARGS: list
    PARALLEL: int
    RUNS: tuple  # each model's startup line: the steps its monokernels run

    @classmethod
    def setUpClass(cls):
        cls.logs = tuple(
            tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile("w+", suffix=s) for s in (".out", ".err")
        )
        cls.process = _launch(
            cls.SERVER_ARGS, extra_args=["--watchdog-timeout", "600"], log=cls.logs
        )

    @classmethod
    def tearDownClass(cls):
        if getattr(cls, "process", None) is not None:
            terminate_and_kill_process_tree(cls.process)
        for log in getattr(cls, "logs", ()):
            log.close()

    def test_the_tested_batches_run_the_monokernels(self):
        # routing is fixed at startup; without this, the other tests could pass on
        # the normal path alone
        log = "".join(Path(f.name).read_text() for f in self.logs)
        for line in self.RUNS:
            self.assertIn(line, log)

    def test_gsm8k_past_the_largest_width(self):
        args = SimpleNamespace(
            num_shots=8,
            data_path=None,
            num_questions=200,
            parallel=self.PARALLEL,
            max_new_tokens=512,
            host="127.0.0.1",
            port=int(DEFAULT_URL_FOR_TEST.split(":")[-1]),
        )
        metrics = run_eval_few_shot_gsm8k(args)
        print(f"{metrics=}")
        self.assertGreater(metrics["accuracy"], GSM8K_BOUND)

    def test_covered_steps_match_prefill(self):
        # 8 requests in one batch: every decode or verify step runs at a covered
        # width, and the prefill that scores the tokens again is the normal path
        assert_logprobs_match(
            DEFAULT_URL_FOR_TEST,
            {MODEL: {"kl_div": KL_BOUND}},
            MODEL,
            max_samples=8,
            max_new_tokens=256,
            trust_remote_code=True,
        )


class TestMonokernelVerify(_Serving, CustomTestCase):
    """DSpark verify steps: above 8 requests (48 rows) the normal path."""

    SERVER_ARGS, PARALLEL = ARGS, 12
    RUNS = (
        "monokernel deepseek_v41_hip on gfx950 runs target_verify steps of batch "
        "size [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8] x 6 tokens",
        "monokernel deepseek_v41_dspark_draft_hip on gfx950 runs target_verify steps "
        "of batch size [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8",
    )

    def test_long_prompts_match_prefill(self):
        # past the candidate span every verify step is two-level: the candidate
        # source scores the whole context and keeps its best blocks, the index
        # sources after it score only those (K2i's three launch kinds)
        prompts = _long_prompts()
        decoded = _logprobs(input_ids=prompts, max_new_tokens=128, logprob_start_len=-1)
        outputs = [
            [x[0] for x in r["meta_info"]["output_token_logprobs"]] for r in decoded
        ]
        # the same tokens scored again by a prefill of prompt and output
        full = [p + r["output_ids"] for p, r in zip(prompts, decoded)]
        prefill = _logprobs(input_ids=full, max_new_tokens=0, logprob_start_len=0)
        inputs = [
            [x[0] for x in r["meta_info"]["input_token_logprobs"]][-len(o) :]
            for r, o in zip(prefill, outputs)
        ]
        compare_kl_divergence(
            input_logprobs=inputs,
            output_logprobs=outputs,
            ACC_THRESHOLDS={MODEL: {"kl_div": LONG_KL_BOUND}},
            model_name=MODEL,
            test_name="long prompts",
        )

    def test_passkey_past_the_candidate_span(self):
        # a fact early in a prompt past the candidate span: the candidate source
        # must keep its block for the index sources after it to read it
        from sglang.srt.utils.hf_transformers_utils import get_tokenizer

        tok = get_tokenizer(MODEL, trust_remote_code=True)
        prompt = _long_prompts()[1]
        cut = len(prompt) // 5
        needle = tok.encode(
            f" The passkey is {PASSKEY}. Remember it: {PASSKEY}. ",
            add_special_tokens=False,
        )
        question = tok.encode(
            " What is the passkey? The passkey is", add_special_tokens=False
        )
        r = requests.post(
            DEFAULT_URL_FOR_TEST + "/generate",
            json={
                "input_ids": prompt[:cut] + needle + prompt[cut:] + question,
                "sampling_params": {"temperature": 0, "max_new_tokens": 16},
            },
            timeout=600,
        )
        text = r.json()["text"]
        print(f"passkey answer: {text!r}")
        self.assertIn(PASSKEY, text)

class TestMonokernelFault(CustomTestCase):
    def test_a_stalled_rank_stops_the_server_without_tokens(self):
        # past startup (5000 launches), rank 1 stalls at its first wait; at the
        # deadline (half the watchdog) it stops, and its peers stop on its flag
        with (
            tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile("w+", suffix=".out") as out,
            tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile("w+", suffix=".err") as err,
        ):
            process = _launch(
                extra_env={"SGLANG_AMD_MONO_FAULT_INJECT": "1:1:5000"},
                extra_args=["--watchdog-timeout", "20"],
                log=(out, err),
            )
            try:
                try:
                    r = requests.post(
                        DEFAULT_URL_FOR_TEST + "/generate",
                        json={
                            "text": "Write a long essay about lighthouses.",
                            "sampling_params": {
                                "max_new_tokens": 1024,
                                "temperature": 0,
                                "ignore_eos": True,
                            },
                        },
                        timeout=300,
                    )
                    ok = r.status_code == 200 and r.json().get("text")
                except requests.RequestException:
                    ok = False
                self.assertFalse(ok, "a failed step's tokens reached the client")
                deadline = time.time() + 300
                while process.poll() is None and time.time() < deadline:
                    time.sleep(2)
                self.assertIsNotNone(process.poll(), "the server kept running")
                err.seek(0)
                out.seek(0)
                log = err.read() + out.read()
                # a launch never runs on after a failed wait: it stops with a store
                # to the null page, so the only faults are at address 0x0, none on
                # words that never came
                faults = re.findall(r"faulting addr: (0x[0-9a-fA-F]+)", log)
                self.assertTrue(faults, log[-2000:])
                self.assertEqual(set(faults) - {"0x0"}, set(), faults)
            finally:
                terminate_and_kill_process_tree(process)

"""The GLM-5.3 gfx950 monokernel spec on CPU (RFC #43949): the layers its forward
covers on the GLM-5.3 layer structure, its row routing and TP4 row cap, its registry
entry, and its config and model refusal reasons. SGLang checks its declared
requirements, the same way for every spec."""

from types import SimpleNamespace

import pytest
import torch
from sglang.srt.layers.moe.utils import MoeRunnerBackend
from sglang.srt.monokernels import spec as registry

import sgl_amd_mono
from sgl_amd_mono.glm53 import HF_CONFIG
from sgl_amd_mono.glm53 import spec as glm53
from sgl_amd_mono.glm53.gfx950.weights import rope_tables

# GLM-5.3's layer structure and quantization (its config.json)
GLM53 = SimpleNamespace(
    **HF_CONFIG,
    num_hidden_layers=78,
    first_k_dense_replace=3,
    moe_layer_freq=1,
    quantization_config={"quant_method": "fp8", "weight_block_size": [128, 128]},
    rope_parameters={"rope_theta": 8000000, "rope_type": "default"},
    architectures=["GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM"],
)


def test_the_forward_covers_the_moe_layers():
    # the dense layers 0 to 2 run SGLang's path inside the forward
    assert glm53._covered_layers(GLM53) == list(range(3, 78))


def test_the_plugin_registers_the_spec():
    # what SGLang's load_plugins() runs, from the sglang.srt.plugins entry point
    sgl_amd_mono.register_specs()
    arch = ["GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM"]
    found, why = registry.find_spec(
        backend=sgl_amd_mono.BACKEND, architectures=arch, isa="gfx950"
    )
    assert found is glm53.SPEC, why
    found, why = registry.find_spec(
        backend=sgl_amd_mono.BACKEND, architectures=arch, isa="gfx942"
    )
    assert found is None and "gfx942" in why


class _Lm:
    """A model whose own forward records that it ran."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.model, self.ran = SimpleNamespace(), []

    def forward(self, *args):
        self.ran.append(args)
        return "the model's forward"


def test_a_step_runs_at_the_next_width_and_tp4_takes_four_rows():
    # a one-row launch never completes on gfx950: one row runs at width 2
    assert [glm53._width(r) for r in glm53.ROWS] == [2, 2, 4, 4, 8, 8, 8, 8]
    # TP4 builds no 8-row launch: a wider step runs the model's own forward
    runtimes = {(w, k): None for w in (2, 4) for k in ("index", "shared")}
    layers = {i: SimpleNamespace(i=i) for i in range(3, 78)}
    lm = _Lm()
    built = glm53._Built(lm, layers, runtimes, None, None, tp=4, device="cpu")
    key = registry.ShapeKey(forward_mode="decode", batch_size=5, tokens_per_request=1)
    out = built.forward(registry.Plan(key=key), "ids", "positions", "batch")
    assert out == "the model's forward"
    assert lm.ran == [("ids", "positions", "batch", None, None)]
    assert (
        glm53._Built(lm, layers, runtimes, None, None, tp=8, device="cpu").max_rows == 8
    )


def test_config_reasons_name_each_mismatch():
    cfg = SimpleNamespace(page_size=None)
    assert glm53._config_disable_reasons(cfg, GLM53) == []
    other = SimpleNamespace(
        **{
            **vars(GLM53),
            "index_topk_freq": 8,
            "moe_layer_freq": 2,
            "quantization_config": {"quant_method": "quark"},
            "rope_parameters": {"rope_type": "yarn", "factor": 4.0},
        }
    )
    reasons = glm53._config_disable_reasons(SimpleNamespace(page_size=1), other)
    text = " ".join(reasons)
    assert "index_topk_freq" in text
    assert "MoE" in text
    assert "--page-size 1" in text
    assert "FP8 block-128" in text
    assert "RoPE 'yarn'" in text


def _linear(shuffled=True):
    # SGLang marks only the block-FP8 linears it rewrote into AITER's layout
    if not shuffled:
        return SimpleNamespace(weight=SimpleNamespace())
    return SimpleNamespace(
        aiter_bpreshuffled=True, weight=SimpleNamespace(is_shuffled=True)
    )


def _layer(
    experts_dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn,
    n_experts=257,
    indexer=True,
    shuffled=True,
    runner=MoeRunnerBackend.AITER,
    fused_indexer=True,
):
    w13 = torch.empty(n_experts, 1, 1, dtype=experts_dtype)
    quant = SimpleNamespace(runner=SimpleNamespace(runner_backend=runner))
    ind = SimpleNamespace(
        wq_b=_linear(), wk=_linear(), use_gfx950_fused_indexer=fused_indexer
    )
    attn = SimpleNamespace(
        fused_qkv_a_proj_with_mqa=_linear(shuffled),
        q_b_proj=_linear(),
        o_proj=_linear(),
        indexer=ind if indexer else None,
    )
    experts = SimpleNamespace(w13_weight=w13, quant_method=quant)
    return SimpleNamespace(mlp=SimpleNamespace(experts=experts), self_attn=attn)


def _model(layers):
    return SimpleNamespace(model=SimpleNamespace(layers=layers))


def _layers():
    # GLM-5.3's indexers: layers 0 to 2, then every fourth from layer 6
    return [_layer(indexer=i % 4 == 2 or i < 3) for i in range(78)]


def test_model_reasons():
    good = _layers()
    assert glm53._model_disable_reasons(_model(good), GLM53, {}) == []
    bad = list(good)
    bad[5] = _layer(experts_dtype=torch.bfloat16)
    bad[9] = _layer(n_experts=256)
    bad[2] = _layer(indexer=False)
    reasons = " ".join(glm53._model_disable_reasons(_model(bad), GLM53, {}))
    assert "layer 5: needs block-FP8 experts" in reasons
    assert "layer 9: needs the shared expert fused" in reasons
    assert "layer 3 reuses the top-k of layer 2" in reasons


def test_model_reasons_name_the_layouts_the_kernel_cannot_read():
    # These served wrong tokens without a refusal: the kernel read row-major FP8
    # projections (--fp8-gemm-backend triton) and experts off the AITER MoE
    # runner as (16, 16) tiles, and scored rotated index queries against keys that
    # an indexer other than SGLang's gfx950 fused one caches unrotated
    layers = _layers()
    layers[4] = _layer(indexer=False, shuffled=False)
    layers[5] = _layer(indexer=False, shuffled=False)
    layers[7] = _layer(indexer=False, runner=MoeRunnerBackend.TRITON)
    layers[10] = _layer(fused_indexer=False)
    reasons = glm53._model_disable_reasons(_model(layers), GLM53, {})
    assert [r.split(":")[0] for r in reasons] == [
        "layer 7",
        "fused_qkv_a_proj_with_mqa of 2 layers from 4",
        "the indexer of layer 10",
    ], reasons
    assert "AITER MoE runner" in reasons[0] and "(16, 16)" in reasons[1]
    assert "gfx950 fused DSA indexer" in reasons[2]


def test_every_indexer_rotary_must_equal_the_mla_one():
    # The first covered layer reuses layer 2's top-k and has no indexer, so an
    # indexer rotary unlike the MLA one went unchecked
    table = torch.randn(16, 64)

    def layer(indexer_table=None):
        rotary = SimpleNamespace(cos_sin_cache=table)
        indexer = None
        if indexer_table is not None:
            indexer = SimpleNamespace(
                rotary_emb=SimpleNamespace(cos_sin_cache=indexer_table)
            )
        return SimpleNamespace(
            self_attn=SimpleNamespace(rotary_emb=rotary, indexer=indexer)
        )

    cos, _ = rope_tables([layer(), layer(table.clone())], {})
    assert torch.equal(cos, table[:, :32].to(torch.bfloat16))
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="indexer's rotary"):
        rope_tables([layer(), layer(table + 1)], {})
